evidence: createApp() calls express() and app.use(express.json()). This is framework setup, which belongs in infrastructure.
createApp() creates InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository, and passes them into the use cases. This is dependency wiring, which belongs in the composition root.

The app.post('/projects', ...), app.post('/tasks', ...) and app.get('/projects/:projectId/tasks', ...) calls map HTTP routes to controllers. This is transport routing, which belongs in infrastructure.
seedUsers() saves fixed sample User instances through userRepository.save. This is seed data for the in-memory store, not business logic.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/infrastructure/app.ts is the composition root, and that role belongs to the infrastructure layer. It sets up Express (the framework and the JSON middleware) and creates the in-memory repository adapters. It wires the application use cases into the controllers and maps HTTP routes to controller methods. All of these are framework, transport and wiring tasks. The seedUsers helper puts fixed sample users into the in-memory repository. That is setup of data for the infrastructure, not a business rule: it doesn't check invariants or make domain decisions. The file contains no business logic, validation or domain rules, so its responsibilities fit the infrastructure layer.
